title: Traditional Chinese Medicine Industry Leigong Large Model
summary: The Leigong submission reports faster herbal sorting, lower Poria return costs, and improved knowledge access, alongside proposed health benefits.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: Huawei and Yunnan Baiyao describe a traditional Chinese medicine model spanning cultivation, production, research, and guidance. The submission associates AI applications with 30–50-fold sorting-efficiency gains, CNY 50 million lower annual Poria return costs, and 30–50% higher patient satisfaction. It does not specify the measurement methods or isolate each result to one deployment. Health effects remain unmeasured.
purpose: Improve knowledge use and operational decisions across the TCM supply chain.
system: Leigong large model for traditional Chinese medicine
developer: Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd. and Yunnan Baiyao Group Co., Ltd.

ratings.reason: The submission reports improved sorting accuracy and 30–50-fold efficiency gains, plus lower Poria return costs; the system-specific attribution and baseline definitions remain unclear.
The submission claims a 30–50% improvement in patient satisfaction with the knowledge service; no survey design or health outcome is supplied.
Global acceptance of traditional medicine is an asserted aim, not a measured population outcome.

ai_role.statement: The account does not isolate AI’s contribution from the surrounding workflow.

evidence.citation: International Telecommunication Union, AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025). Project-submitted account, current as of June 2025. ITU provides no independent outcome evaluation.
evidence.title: Use Case 16: Traditional Chinese Medicine Industry Leigong Large Model

produced_by: The account does not establish conditions sufficient to reproduce the benefit.
must_hold: The account does not establish requirements for reproducing the benefit in other settings.

headline: Leigong links TCM knowledge with cultivation and production
claim_basis: Sources: the makers' report. The cited evidence includes no independent source and no finding by a regulator or court.
